statement: In 6 of 8 analysed books framed by bedtime or sleep, the last page returns to the opening place or image at low intensity (0-2 of 5) after a peak earlier in the book (Good Night, Monu; Bathtub Safari; Zuko and the crying tap; Goodnight, Tinku!; A House for Mouse; Clever Pig); Bohlale's adventure ends on a high payoff (4 of 5) and Kottavi Raja ends calm but in a different place, after a late second peak.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-15: from three sources (Book Dash: Bathtub Safari, Zuko; StoryWeaver: Good Night, Monu; African Storybook: Bohlale as counterexample). Final-page intensity 1/5 (Monu, Bathtub Safari), 2/5 (Zuko), 4/5 (Bohlale); on the engine's 0-3 scale about 0-1 for the three, 2-3 for Bohlale. Monu and Bathtub Safari peak at or before the midpoint and then descend, so this is a shape where the peak is not in the last third (see c_peak_in_last_third). Small sample; inferred from intensity judgments. 2026-10-20 (answering q_uyku_oncesi): Goodnight, Tinku! (StoryWeaver, Pratham Books) opens and closes with the pup by his sleeping mother under the same smiling moon, final page 0/5; its excitement is a plateau p4-p8 of 11 (engine about 2), the last peak page at 0.73, so on m006's definition it would not pass a 'peak by two thirds' check. Kottavi Raja (Pratham, 7-8) is a counterexample: last peak p16 of 17.
2026-10-28: +2 Book Dash. Clever Pig returns to the sty, the play invitation and the carrot, now full of piglets, at 1/5. A House for Mouse returns only visually (the closing picture repeats the cover's hill image; the story ends at a new place, the bookshelf) — counted as support, weakly. Both peak before the last third (m006). Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-11-13: +1 support: Sweet Dreams returns on its last page to the dream world of its first page at 2/5 after a peak at the warm halwa close-up (3/5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale) and a waking turn. Note for the parked proposal: the return is into sleep, not back to the bedroom. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.current: bedtime mode shares beat sequences with the other modes; m004 already keeps hooks out of its last third
magicpaper.suggested: For bedtime blueprints only: place the emotional peak no later than about two thirds through, and let the final page return to the opening setting (bed, room, window) at the lowest intensity of the story.
magicpaper.note: Hypothesis from 4 books; bedtime-specific, does not apply to adventure or learning modes.
